title: apricity-data domain replace_warp_markers and library mode for import
description:
## Intent
Library mode: your warp markers as Marker records.

## Scope
- `crates/apricity-data/src/domain.rs`: `replace_warp_markers(sample_id, markers, identity) -> Result<Replaced{added, removed}>`: deletes the identity's `warp` markers for the sample and creates the new ones (`source: user`, `beat`), under the library lock (`transact`), idempotent (same set → no writes).
- `apricity-cli` import/reset with `--library` call it; records sync like any marker (no change to sync).
- The `features/data/domain/warp_markers.feature` scenarios green in the Rust runner; the TypeScript runner (apricitus-d121e0) gets a matching step only if the domain op is exposed to the web (not in this task; note it).

## Verify
`safe-run.sh -- cargo test -p apricity-data` and the library scenarios of `cargo test -p apricity-cli --test daw_cli`.

Commit: `feat(<this id>): replace warp markers in a library`.

---
**Toolchain:** every Bash call starts with `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`; run builds and tests under the watchdog: `safe-run.sh -- <command>` (6 GB / 20 min cap; do not edit it). At most two Rust-building agents at once.
**Protocol:** specs first (write the scenario, watch it fail, then code); keep a running log with `kbs comment` (decisions, problems, attempts, outcomes); paste the tail of **Verify** before asking for review; never commit, push or close (the reviewer does, after re-running Verify). Never write the DAW's brand name anywhere.
